en: 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to me: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah: He heard 'Uqbah ibn 'Abd al-Ghafir saying: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrating from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "There was a man among those who were before you to whom Allah had granted wealth and children. He said to his children: 'You must certainly do what I command you to do, or else I will assign my inheritance to other than you. When I die, burn me'—and to the best of my knowledge he said—'then grind me and scatter me in the wind, for I have not preserved any good with Allah, and if Allah takes hold of me He will punish me.' He said: So he took a covenant from them, and they did that to him, by my Lord! Then Allah said: 'What prompted you to do what you did?' He said: 'Fear of You.' He said: And nothing spared him except that."

Abu al-Rabi' Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us: Al-Zubaydi narrated to me: Al-Zuhri said: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "A servant transgressed against himself..." similar to the hadith of Ma'mar up to his words: "so Allah forgave him." And he did not mention the hadith of the woman in the story of the cat. And in the hadith of al-Zubaydi, he said: "So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to everything that took something from him: 'Deliver up what you took from him.'"

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us; 'Abd said: He informed us, and Ibn Rafi' said—and the wording is his: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Al-Zuhri said to me: Shall I not narrate to you two wondrous hadiths? Al-Zuhri said: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "A man transgressed against himself, and when death approached him, he instructed his sons, saying: 'When I die, burn me, then grind me, then scatter me in the wind into the sea; for, by Allah, if my Lord takes hold of me, He will surely punish me with a punishment with which He has not punished anyone.' He said: So they did that to him. Then He said to the earth: 'Deliver up what you took.' And lo, he was standing upright. He said to him: 'What prompted you to do what you did?' He said: 'Fear of You, O Lord'—or he said—'fear of You.' So He forgave him because of that." Al-Zuhri said: And Humayd narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "A woman entered the Fire on account of a cat that she tied up; she neither fed it nor released it to eat from the vermin of the earth, until it died of starvation." Al-Zuhri said: That is so that no man should rely complacently, nor should any man despair.

Muhammad ibn Marzuq, grandson of the daughter of Mahdi ibn Maymun, narrated to me: Rawh narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "A man who had never done any good said to his family: 'When he dies, burn him, then scatter half of him on land and half of him in the sea; for, by Allah, if Allah takes hold of him, He will surely punish him with a punishment with which He does not punish anyone in the worlds.' When the man died, they did what he commanded them. Then Allah commanded the land, and it gathered what was in it, and He commanded the sea, and it gathered what was in it. Then He said: 'Why did you do this?' He said: 'Out of fear of You, O Lord, and You know best.' So Allah forgave him."

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr all narrated to us from Isma'il ibn Ja'far; Ibn Ayyub said: Isma'il narrated to us: Al-'Ala' informed me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "If the believer knew what is with Allah of punishment, no one would covet His Paradise; and if the disbeliever knew what is with Allah of mercy, no one would despair of His Paradise."

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Tamimi—and the wording is Hasan's—narrated to me: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Abu Ghassan narrated to us: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me, from his father, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, that he said: Some captives were brought to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and there was a woman among the captives searching [for her child]. When she found an infant among the captives, she took it, pressed it to her belly, and suckled it. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to us: "Do you think this woman would throw her child into the fire?" We said: "No, by Allah, while she is able not to throw it." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah is surely more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child."

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu 'Uthman, from Salman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, on the day He created the heavens and the earth, Allah created one hundred mercies, each mercy spanning what is between the heaven and the earth. He placed one mercy thereof on the earth, and through it the mother shows compassion to her child, and the wild beasts and birds show compassion to one another. When the Day of Resurrection comes, He will complete them with this mercy."
And Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated it to us: Al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, with this chain of transmission.

Al-Hakam ibn Musa narrated to me: Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us: Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi narrated to us, from Salman al-Farsi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Allah has one hundred mercies; among them is one mercy by which creation shows mercy among themselves, and ninety-nine are for the Day of Resurrection."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us: 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Indeed, Allah has one hundred mercies. He sent down one mercy thereof among the jinn, humans, beasts, and vermin, by which they show affection, by which they show mercy to one another, and by which the wild beast shows compassion to its child; and Allah has reserved ninety-nine mercies with which He will show mercy to His servants on the Day of Resurrection."

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr said: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah created one hundred mercies; He placed one among His creation and concealed with Himself one hundred less one."

Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed him that Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Allah made mercy into one hundred parts. He kept ninety-nine parts with Himself and sent down one single part to the earth. From that single part, all creatures show mercy to one another, until a mare lifts its hoof from its foal out of fear that it might harm it."

Ali ibn Khashram narrated to us: Abu Damrah informed us, from al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ata' ibn Mina', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When Allah decreed the creation, He wrote in His Book upon Himself, and it is placed with Him: 'Indeed, My mercy prevails over My wrath.'"

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'My mercy has preceded My wrath.'"

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Al-Mughirah—meaning al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When Allah created the creation, He wrote in His Book, which is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed, My mercy prevails over My wrath.'"

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Hanzalah al-Tamimi al-Usayyidi, the scribe, who said: We were with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he reminded us of Paradise and the Fire... and he mentioned similar to their hadith.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: 'Abd al-Samad informed us: I heard my father narrating: Sa'id al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Hanzalah, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he admonished us and reminded [us of] the Fire. He said: Then I came to the house, laughed with the children, and played with the woman (my wife). He said: Then I went out and met Abu Bakr, and I mentioned that to him. He said: "And I have done the like of what you mention." So we met the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, Hanzalah has become a hypocrite!" He said: "Hold on!" So I narrated the account to him. Then Abu Bakr said: "And I have done the like of what he did." He said: "O Hanzalah, an hour and an hour; and if your hearts remained as they are during the remembrance, the angels would shake hands with you until they greet you with peace in the streets."

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi and Qatan ibn Nusayr—and the wording is Yahya's—narrated to us; Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us, from Sa'id ibn Iyas al-Jurayri, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Hanzalah al-Usayyidi—he said: and he was one of the scribes of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—who said: Abu Bakr met me and said: "How are you, O Hanzalah?" He said: I said: "Hanzalah has become a hypocrite." He said: "Subhan Allah! What are you saying?" He said: I said: "We are in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); he reminds us of the Fire and Paradise until it is as though we see them with our own eyes. But when we leave the presence of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), we busy ourselves with our wives, children, and properties, and we forget much." Abu Bakr said: "By Allah, we also experience the like of this." So I and Abu Bakr set off until we entered upon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). I said: "Hanzalah has become a hypocrite, O Messenger of Allah!" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "And what is that?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are in your presence and you remind us of the Fire and Paradise until it is as though we see them with our own eyes. But when we leave your presence, we busy ourselves with our wives, children, and properties, and we forget much." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, if you were to remain constantly in the state you are in while with me and in remembrance, the angels would shake hands with you on your beds and in your paths; but, O Hanzalah, an hour and an hour"—three times.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Ja'far al-Jazari, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, if you did not commit sins, Allah would do away with you and bring a people who commit sins, so that they seek forgiveness from Allah and He forgives them."

Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: 'Iyad—and he is Ibn 'Abdullah al-Fihri—narrated to me: Ibrahim ibn 'Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abu Sirmah, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "Were it not that you had sins that Allah forgives for you, Allah would bring a people who have sins that He forgives for them."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays—the storyteller of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz—from Abu Sirmah, from Abu Ayyub, that he said when death approached him: I had concealed from you something that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Were it not that you commit sins, Allah would create a creation who commit sins and He forgives them."

Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah is surely more pleased with the repentance of His servant than one of you when he awakens finding his camel which he had lost in a desolate land." And Ahmad al-Darimi narrated it to me: Habban narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah and Zuhayr ibn Harb both narrated to us: 'Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah narrated to us: Anas ibn Malik—and he was his uncle—narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah is surely more pleased with the repentance of His servant when he repents to Him than one of you who was on his riding camel in a desert land and it escaped from him carrying his food and drink, so he despaired of it. He came to a tree and lay down in its shade, having despaired of his riding camel. While he was in that state, lo, it was standing right before him! So he took hold of its nose-rope and then said out of extreme joy: 'O Allah, You are my servant and I am your Lord!' He erred out of extreme joy."

Yahya ibn Yahya and Ja'far ibn Humayd narrated to us; Ja'far said: He narrated to us, and Yahya said: 'Ubaydullah ibn Iyad ibn Laqit informed us, from Iyad, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "What do you say about the joy of a man whose riding camel escaped from him, dragging its halter in a barren land in which there is neither food nor drink, while bearing for him his food and drink; so he searched for it until it became exhausting for him, then it passed by the stump of a tree and its halter got caught, so he found it entangled by it?" We said: "Very great joy, O Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, by Allah, Allah is surely more pleased with the repentance of His servant than the man with his riding camel." Ja'far said: 'Ubaydullah ibn Iyad narrated to us from his father.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Abu Yunus narrated to us, from Simak, who said: Al-Nu'man ibn Bashir delivered a sermon and said: "Allah is surely more pleased with the repentance of His servant than a man who loaded his provisions and water skin onto a camel, then journeyed until he reached a desolate land; then the midday heat overtook him, so he dismounted and took a midday nap under a tree. Sleep overcame him and his camel slipped away. He woke up and ran up an elevated hill, but saw nothing; then he ran up a second elevated hill, but saw nothing; then he ran up a third elevated hill, but saw nothing. So he returned until he reached the spot where he had taken his midday nap. While he was sitting, suddenly his camel came walking toward him until it placed its halter into his hand. Surely Allah is more pleased with the repentance of the servant than this man when he found his camel in its state." Simak said: Al-Sha'bi claimed that al-Nu'man attributed this hadith to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), but as for me, I did not hear it [attributed to him].

And Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Al-A'mash narrated to us: 'Umarah ibn 'Umayr narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Harith ibn Suwayd saying: 'Abdullah narrated to me two hadiths: one of them from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and the other from himself. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah is surely more pleased with the repentance of His believing servant..." similar to the hadith of Jarir.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Qutbah ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from al-A'mash with this chain of transmission, and he said: "than a man in an open, desolate wasteland."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim—and the wording is 'Uthman's—narrated to us; Ishaq said: Jarir informed us, and 'Uthman said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Umarah ibn 'Umayr, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, who said: I visited 'Abdullah to inquire about him while he was ill, so he narrated to us two hadiths: a hadith from himself and a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Allah is surely more pleased with the repentance of His believing servant than a man in a perilous desert wasteland with whom was his riding camel bearing his food and drink; he slept and then awakened to find it had gone. He searched for it until thirst overtook him, then he said: 'I will return to my place where I was and sleep until I die.' So he placed his head upon his forearm to die, then he awakened and there was his riding camel beside him bearing his provisions, food, and drink. For Allah is more pleased with the repentance of the believing servant than this man with his riding camel and his provisions."

Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Tamimi, 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bahram, and Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me; Ibn Sahl said: He narrated to us, and the other two said: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: Salim ibn 'Abdullah informed me that 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Three persons from among those who were before you set out until the approach of night drove them to a cave..." and he related the hadith with the meaning of the hadith of Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar, except that he said: One of the men said: "O Allah, I had elderly, aged parents, and I never used to give evening milk to family or wealth before them." And he said: "So she refused me until a year of hardship struck her, so she came to me and I gave her one hundred and twenty dinars." And he said: "So I invested his wage until wealth multiplied from it and spread out abundantly." And he said: "So they exited the cave walking."

And Ishaq ibn Mansur and 'Abd ibn Humayd both narrated to us: Abu 'Asim informed us, from Ibn Jurayj: Musa ibn 'Uqbah informed me; (H) and Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah; (H) and Abu Kurayb and Muhammad ibn Tarif al-Bajali both narrated to me: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us: My father and Raqabah ibn Masqalah narrated to us; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb, Hasan al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me, saying: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd—narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan; all of them from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with the meaning of the hadith of Abu Damrah from Musa ibn 'Uqbah. And they added in their hadith: "and they exited walking." And in the hadith of Salih: "walking together." Except 'Ubaydullah, for in his hadith it is: "and they exited," and he mentioned nothing after it.
